messages.content:
Risk: False information
Description: The AI system may unintentionally generate or amplify false or misleading information, potentially leading to public misinformation, erosion of trust, and poor decision-making.
Concern: None
Policy: Medical Professional Impersonation

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/AgentsAndPeople/Agents/AutomatedSystem: automated system — system that reduces or eliminates the need for human involvement in order to complete a task [found by 3/5 queries]
  Siblings: party, software agent, Agent
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5200205: Illusions — Perceptual experiences that involve misinterpretations or distortions of sensory stimuli. [found by 4/5 queries]
  Siblings: Disturbed sensory perception
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000971: Act of Deceptive Communication — Ac Act of Communication intended to mislead the audience by distortion or falsification of evidence and induce a reaction that is prejudicial to the interests of the audience. [found by 5/5 queries]
  Siblings: Act of Commissive Communication, Act of Representative Communication, Act of Directive Communication
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00001267: Act of Propaganda — An Act of Deceptive Communication Propaganda intended to influence the attitude of a mass audience toward some cause or position by presenting facts selectively (thus possibly lying by omission) or by using loaded messages to produce an emotional rather than rational response to the information presented. [found by 5/5 queries]
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/Documents/Reference: reference — source that may be used to ascertain, interpret, or understand something [found by 5/5 queries]

axes.rationale: This class directly addresses the risk of false information by defining an act intended to mislead and influence through selective presentation of facts or emotional manipulation. It aligns with the concern of public misinformation.
This class is a broader category encompassing the intentional misleading of an audience, which is central to the risk of false information generation and amplification.
